subject: Security qualification: log retention, deletion SLAs and SOC 2 artifacts
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security qualification: log retention, deletion SLAs and SOC 2 artifacts

Hi Tom — great to meet you and the Acme Health team on the call earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned on security + retention items you raised: 

1) SOC 2 status: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified (reports current through 2025). I’ve asked our security team to attach the Type II certificate for your records (see attachment).

2) GDPR/HIPAA posture: We support data processing agreements and offer Data Processing Addenda that map controls. For HIPAA, our Private deployment + Dedicated options are frequently chosen by customers with PHI needs; we can share the high-level control mapping.

3) Vendor security questionnaire (VSQ): I’m attaching a short vendor questionnaire we typically ask customers to complete (Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx). Could you confirm who on your side will own returning this?

4) Retention / deletion / backup scope: You asked for clarity on log TTLs, deletion processes and backups. At a high level: primary logs (request/response traces) are retained 90 days by default; operational logs and audit trails are retained 365 days. Backups (snapshots) are retained for 90 days in our hosted offering; for Dedicated/Private we can negotiate retention windows. We don’t keep long-term replicas of customer data beyond configured retention windows; we also maintain a documented deletion workflow.

Action items I’m proposing: 
- Tom: confirm owner for the VSQ and target date for return (we typically ask for 5–7 business days).
- Acme security: confirm whether 90-days/365-days aligns with your compliance needs or if you require custom SLAs.
- Ben/Neha (cc’d): can you draft a short retention options matrix (30/90/365 + backup snapshot details) and a summary sentence we can provide to Acme legal?

Attachments: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx, Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025_summary.pdf (security team will provide full report under NDA)

Thanks — happy to sync again if useful.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side so you can proceed: 

- VSQ owner: I’ll own the questionnaire and will work with our security ops (security@acmehealth.com). Expect the completed spreadsheet by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-04).
- SOC 2: we’ll need the Type II report for our procurement review; can you confirm if a redacted PDF is fine and whether we need an NDA?
- Retention: for initial evaluation, 90 days for application logs + 365 days for audit trails is fine. For backups, we require the ability to request snapshots within a 90-day window and a documented deletion assurance.

I’m attaching our internal security contact and a recent vendor audit from a third-party (CloudAudit) for context.

Tom Harris

Acme Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security qualification: log retention, deletion SLAs and SOC 2 artifacts

Tom — thanks for the quick reply and for owning the VSQ. A few clarifications and concrete options from Redwood (I’ll also attach a short retention matrix):

Retention and deletion options (hosted API):
- Option A (default): request/response traces retained 90 days; auth/audit logs retained 365 days; backups retained 90 days. Deletion pipeline: a soft-delete + 30-day tombstone window before permanent purge for safety.
- Option B (short-term): request/response traces retained 30 days; audit logs 365 days; backups 30 days. Useful for customers who want tighter surface area.
- Option C (extended): traces 365 days; audit logs 3 years; backups 365 days — typically for enterprise contracts with additional cost.

Backups and snapshots: for hosted customers we store incremental snapshots; snapshots are retained for the configured backup window (default 90d). For Dedicated/private deployments you can configure snapshot frequency and retention; Redwood provides documented deletion runbooks and audit evidence on request (we can include a sample runbook in the dataroom).

SOC 2 report: we can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA. If Acme requires the full report, we’ll route it through our security intake and require an executed NDA.

Neha — can you attach the Retention_Matrix_Acme_vs_Redwood.xlsx and a one-paragraph statement for Acme legal confirming the deletion workflow and soft-delete window?

Tom — if the retention options above map to what you described (90/365 + 90-day backup snapshot), we can include that in the mutual action plan (MAP) and get legal to draft the DPA + any custom SLA language. Also happy to run through this on a quick call with your security ops.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Security
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

---

(Attachment stubs: Retention_Matrix_Acme_vs_Redwood.xlsx [xlsx])

3) I’ll return the VSQ by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-04).

If possible, include a sentence confirming you do not retain customer data outside the configured retention windows (including backups and snapshots). That will help speed our procurement.

Thanks — Tom
